case-sara.text: [Softly] Seeing his name pop up still throws me, and I hate how much it matters.
case-sara.suggestion: Seeing his name still throws you, and the painful part is how much it still matters. Stay right at admitting that it matters and notice what stirs.

case-sara.text: [Embarrassed] I tell friends I'm fine, and then I worry they can hear that I am not.
case-sara.suggestion: You try to sound fine, and it feels risky that they might hear how not fine you are. Find the moment when being heard starts to feel dangerous.

case-sara.text: [Tearful] I feel lost after the breakup, like I do not know what to do with the evenings.
case-sara.suggestion: The evenings are where the lostness shows up most clearly. Bring one evening close and sense what feels hardest when there is nowhere to put yourself.

case-sara.text: [Softly] I wrote 'sorry' to him three times, then realized I do not know what I was trying to fix.
case-sara.suggestion: Writing sorry was a reach toward repair, and then the ground disappeared under what you were trying to fix. Slow down at that unclear place and see which feeling appears.

case-sara.text: [Panicked] I delete photos to prove I am done, then panic and look for them again.
case-sara.suggestion: One move says, 'be done,' and then the panic says this ending is not that simple. Pause in the moment between deleting and searching.

case-sara.text: [Embarrassed] When someone is kind to me, my eyes drop before I can stop it.
case-sara.suggestion: Kindness arrives, and your eyes go down before you can really take it in. Catch the instant before your eyes drop.

case-sara.text: [Softly] For a few seconds after I wake up, I forget he is gone, and then I remember.
case-sara.suggestion: There is that brief relief, and then the loss returns all at once. Let the moment of remembering be here before you have to do anything with it.

case-sara.text: [Embarrassed] I am sad, and then I get embarrassed that I am still talking about it.
case-sara.suggestion: Sadness is here, and embarrassment quickly asks whether you should still be talking about it. Give both a little room and notice which one is stronger now.

case-sara.text: [Tearful] When I see couples holding hands, I get upset and then feel childish for wanting that.
case-sara.suggestion: Seeing them brings up the wanting, and then shame moves in around the wanting. Keep close to the wanting for a moment before shame moves in.

case-sara.text: [Embarrassed] If I let someone see the whole mess, I imagine them quietly wishing I would stop.
case-sara.suggestion: Part of you wants someone to see how bad it is, and another part expects them to wish you would stop. Track that pull between wanting to be seen and expecting rejection.

case-sara.text: [Tearful] I had something funny to tell him on the bus. For a moment I forgot we weren't together. Remembering was the sad part.
case-sara.suggestion: The sadness arrives when you remember you can't tell him. Could we stay for a moment with how that lands now?

case-sara.text: [Softly] My sister didn't tell me to move on. She just stayed. I felt relieved, and I think there's more to it than that.
case-sara.suggestion: There's relief in her simply staying. Take a little time with that relief and see what else you notice.

case-michael.text: [Firm] When someone corrects one detail, I keep hearing it afterward like I was called out.
case-michael.suggestion: The correction keeps echoing as being called out. Let that exposed feeling have a moment before the anger takes over.

case-michael.text: [Tense and angry] I walk into meetings already ready for somebody to disrespect me.
case-michael.suggestion: You enter already on guard, before anything has happened. Let yourself feel what it is like to walk in already ready for disrespect.

case-michael.text: [Tense] After I blow up at home, I tell myself they pushed me, but I still feel lousy.
case-michael.suggestion: One part says they pushed you, and another part is left with that lousy feeling afterward. Keep close to the lousy feeling before the argument about blame takes over.

case-michael.text: [Ashamed] Sometimes I want to throw my phone after a work message, and then I feel ridiculous.
case-michael.suggestion: The urge comes fast, and then you are left looking at yourself with shame. Pause with the shame that follows, just before it calls you ridiculous.

case-michael.text: [Defensive] A small sigh from my wife can feel like she has already decided I am the problem.
case-michael.suggestion: That small sigh lands like a decision has already been made about you. Slow down at the first flare and notice what it says you are being accused of.

case-michael.text: [Tense] When I do not know the answer, I get tense and start talking like I know anyway.
case-michael.suggestion: Not knowing becomes hard to leave visible. Pause at that tense moment before sounding certain takes over.

case-michael.text: [Ashamed] I reread every message before sending because one mistake will bother me all night.
case-michael.suggestion: One possible mistake can stay with you for hours, so the checking becomes hard to stop. Find the first moment when checking starts to feel necessary.

case-michael.text: [Tense and angry] The second I feel weak, I get angry and hear my dad saying that is exactly the problem.
case-michael.suggestion: 'Weak' brings anger and your father's judgment in very fast. Pause at the instant when weakness first shows up.

case-michael.text: [Ashamed] Some nights I replay every word I said, trying to find where I messed it up.
case-michael.suggestion: You replay every word, looking for the moment you got it wrong. Sense what happens inside when you think you have found the mistake.

case-michael.text: [Vulnerable] I want my son to feel safe around me, and I do not know how to say that without sounding weak.
case-michael.suggestion: You want safety for him so much, and even naming that wish brushes against the old weakness rule. Let the wish itself have a moment before the rule closes around it.

case-michael.text: [Quietly] My son asked whether I'd be at his game. I said yes, but the way he asked made me sad. Like he couldn't quite count on it.
case-michael.suggestion: There's sadness in hearing that uncertainty from him. What is it like to let yourself notice it here, without fixing it straight away?

case-michael.text: [Frustrated, then hesitant] I was furious about the correction. Then I realised I was disappointed in myself as well. That bit is harder to talk about.
case-michael.suggestion: The disappointment in yourself is harder to approach. We can go slowly and stay with just the bit you can put words to.

case-jason.text: [Quietly] When it is my turn to speak, I lose track of what I was going to say.
case-jason.suggestion: When attention turns toward you, the words vanish. Pause at that exact moment and notice what it feels like when everyone is waiting.

case-jason.text: [Hesitant] I hover over send, then delete the text because wanting contact suddenly feels humiliating.
case-jason.suggestion: The wish for contact is there, and humiliation makes the message hard to let exist. Keep the wanting in focus for a moment before the deleting happens.

case-jason.text: [Fearful] I got invited to a birthday party, and part of me was excited, but then I started worrying I would ruin it.
case-jason.suggestion: There is excitement about being invited, and then worry starts to crowd it. Give the excitement a little space before the worry crowds it.

case-jason.text: [Quietly] If I meet someone's eyes too long, I assume they can tell how awkward I am.
case-jason.suggestion: Eye contact starts to feel like they can see the awkwardness you are trying to hide. Hold on the first second of being seen.

case-jason.text: [Embarrassed] After meetings, one small awkward pause can make me cringe for the rest of the day.
case-jason.suggestion: That one pause keeps coming back long after the meeting. Slow it down and notice what the cringe says about how you think you were seen.

case-jason.text: [Anxious] When I walk into a room, I look for the exit before I decide whether to join anyone.
case-jason.suggestion: The exit has to be found first, before joining can even be considered. Track that first scan of the room.

case-jason.text: [Quietly] Before I introduce myself, I start imagining how strange I will sound.
case-jason.suggestion: Even before you speak, the moment is already becoming a test of how you will come across. Pause before the introduction and sense the imagined strangeness.

case-jason.text: [Hesitant] I compare myself to everyone there and always decide I am the least interesting person.
case-jason.suggestion: The comparison ends with you at the bottom, and it hurts before anyone has actually rejected you. Let that hurt have a moment.

case-jason.text: [Blank] Sometimes I pretend to text so small talk does not have to start.
case-jason.suggestion: The phone gives you a way to pause the contact, and a little cover from being put on the spot. See what happens just before you reach for that cover.

case-jason.text: [Quiet and ashamed] I felt lonely on Sunday, but I also ignored two messages.
case-jason.suggestion: Loneliness and pulling back sit side by side. Keep close to the loneliness that is there even while the messages go unanswered.

case-jason.text: [Quietly pleased] They asked me to join them again. I felt pleased when I read it. Then I started worrying about what I'd say.
case-jason.suggestion: Before the worry arrived, there was that pleased feeling. Could we give it a little room and notice what being invited again was like?

case-jason.text: [Hesitant] I wish my friend had waited for me after the meeting. I don't usually admit wishing for things like that. It feels a bit sad saying it.
case-jason.suggestion: Saying you wanted him to wait brings some sadness. You don't have to explain it away; we can listen to what that sadness is like.

case-laura.text: [Slow and flat] Most days are flat, but if sadness flickers I push it down before it spreads.
case-laura.suggestion: Most days are flat, and when sadness flickers you move quickly to contain it. I want to slow down the moment of that flicker and notice what makes it feel unsafe to let it spread.

case-laura.text: [Fearful] Raised voices do not even have to be aimed at me; I just go quiet and wait for it to pass.
case-laura.suggestion: Even when the anger is not directed at you, your whole system goes quiet and waits. We can stay with that waiting just long enough to notice what it is listening for.

case-laura.text: [Tense and guarded] When my neighbor brought soup, I thanked her and then spent the night wondering what she wanted.
case-laura.suggestion: The kindness came, and suspicion came almost with it. I want to pause in the gap between being offered care and having to search for a catch.

case-laura.text: [Flat and guarded] I pour wine after the dishes because the quiet gets loud, and I don't want to hear my own thoughts.
case-laura.suggestion: After the dishes, the quiet gets loud, and wine gives you a way not to hear it. Could we stay for a moment with the quiet before you have to mute it?

case-laura.text: [Distant] I check the locks twice in the morning too, and then feel foolish because nothing happened.
case-laura.suggestion: Even in daylight, checking the locks leaves you caught between fear and feeling foolish. We can slow down the moment before the second check.

case-laura.text: [Ashamed] Even gentle touch makes me jump, and then I hate that my reaction is so obvious.
case-laura.suggestion: Your body jumps before you decide anything, and then shame comes because the reaction was visible. I want to linger with the after-feeling, once someone has seen it.

case-laura.text: [Slow and flat] When good news comes, I can say the right words, but I feel almost nothing.
case-laura.suggestion: The words know how to respond, while the feeling stays out of reach. Maybe we can be with that almost-nothing without making it perform.

case-laura.text: [Distant] Sometimes a song cracks something open, and for a minute I can almost feel the sadness.
case-laura.suggestion: The song reaches through the numbness for a minute. I would like to linger where sadness is almost available, before it slides away.

case-laura.text: [Tense and guarded] When I imagine asking someone to sit with me, I immediately think of all the reasons they should not have to.
case-laura.suggestion: The wish for comfort appears, and immediately the reasons against it line up. We can stay with the wish before it has to defend itself.

case-laura.text: [Slow and flat] I avoid movies with fighting because I don't want to find out what a single shout will do to me.
case-laura.suggestion: Avoiding the movie protects you from discovering what one shout might set off. I want to pause with the not-wanting-to-find-out.

case-laura.text: [Quiet, surprised] My friend left a meal by the door. I didn't have to invite her in or talk. I felt touched, which surprised me.
case-laura.suggestion: You were touched by being cared for without having to let her in. We can stay with a little of that feeling, just as it is.

case-laura.text: [Guarded, with a pause] I don't want to see him again. I still felt sad when he said he'd stopped asking. Those two things don't seem to fit.
case-laura.suggestion: Not wanting contact and feeling sad that he stopped asking are both here. Could we make a little room for the sadness without making it a decision to see him?

case-carlos.text: [Defensive] My wife says she can hear my tone change before I notice anything is wrong.
case-carlos.suggestion: Your tone changes before you know what happened. We can slow the first turn in you, before it is loud enough for her to hear.

case-carlos.text: [Tense] After a fight, I can stand in the hallway not knowing whether to apologize or pretend nothing happened.
case-carlos.suggestion: That hallway moment has repair and escape both available. I would like to stay with the not-knowing before either move wins.

case-carlos.text: [Fearful] If I back off in an argument, I start feeling like I am losing my place, and then I need to push back.
case-carlos.suggestion: Backing off starts to feel like losing your place, and pushing back becomes the way to find it again. We can pause at the first sign that your place is slipping.

case-carlos.text: [Ashamed] My boy's flinch keeps replaying, and I hate that he learned that fear from me.
case-carlos.suggestion: Your son's flinch keeps bringing you back to love and shame at the same time. I want to stay with the ache of seeing fear connected to you.

case-carlos.text: [Tense] When it gets calm after a fight, I start waiting for someone to bring it up again.
case-carlos.suggestion: Even calm feels provisional, as if the fight could restart any second. Maybe we can notice what you are waiting for in that quiet.

case-carlos.text: [Tense and angry] I can feel the pressure building before I throw something, but in that second stopping feels impossible.
case-carlos.suggestion: There is a second where you can feel the pressure building and stopping already seems out of reach. We can stay right at that second, before the object moves.

case-carlos.text: [Defensive] If I let myself be soft, I don't know whether people will respect me or take advantage.
case-carlos.suggestion: Softness raises the question of respect or being used. I want to stay with that uncertainty without pushing you toward either answer.

case-carlos.text: [Angry, clenching fists] When I feel disrespected, I talk louder because I need them to know it got to me.
case-carlos.suggestion: The louder voice is trying to make sure they know it got to you. We can stay with the part that needs the hurt recognized.

case-carlos.text: [Fearful] When I say I want them safe, I feel my anger drop and something softer scare me.
case-carlos.suggestion: When anger drops, the wish for safety is exposed, and that softer place feels frightening. I would like to stay with the wish before you cover it.

case-carlos.text: [Fearful] When I start feeling small in an argument, panic hits and I feel like I have to get bigger fast.
case-carlos.suggestion: Smallness brings panic, then the pressure to get bigger fast. We can slow the first moment of smallness, before the bigger stance takes over.

case-carlos.text: [Low voice] My daughter leaned against me watching television. I didn't say anything. I was glad she stayed there. I'm glad again saying it now.
case-carlos.suggestion: There's gladness here again as you tell me. Let yourself have a moment with what her staying close felt like.

case-carlos.text: [Angry, then slowing] He made the joke in front of everyone. I laughed along. Afterwards I felt hurt, which is harder to admit than being angry.
case-carlos.suggestion: The hurt is harder to show than the anger. We can stay with only as much of that hurt as you want to bring here.

case-nina.text: [Tired] The second I ask for help, guilt rushes in and I want to pull it back.
case-nina.suggestion: The need barely appears before guilt rushes in to erase it. I want to pause before the request is pulled back and notice what needing might cost.

case-nina.text: [Guilty] I keep folding laundry and answering messages so I do not have to feel resentful.
case-nina.suggestion: Keeping busy keeps resentment from having room. We can pause at the moment when stopping would make it audible.

case-nina.text: [Torn] When I say no, I keep explaining until the no almost disappears.
case-nina.suggestion: The no begins clearly, and then explanations thin it out. I would like to stay where the no is still plain and notice what makes it hard to leave there.

case-nina.text: [Tired] Even asking for a small ride comes out with three apologies.
case-nina.suggestion: The apologies arrive before the ride request can stand by itself. Maybe we can linger with the small need before it has to apologize.

case-nina.text: [Guilty] If the kitchen is messy when someone stops by, I feel caught, like they can see I am not keeping up.
case-nina.suggestion: The messy kitchen becomes a moment of being caught, of others seeing you are not keeping up. We can pause where ordinary mess turns into exposure.

case-nina.text: [Torn] When everyone needs me at once, I start saying yes before I know what I actually want.
case-nina.suggestion: Everyone else's needs arrive first, and yes comes before your own wish has a chance. I want to slow down the space just before the yes.

case-nina.text: [Guilty] Sometimes I imagine someone making me tea and telling me to sit down, and then I feel selfish for even picturing it.
case-nina.suggestion: The image of being cared for appears, and selfishness quickly moves in to judge it. We can stay with the cared-for wish before the judgment arrives.

case-nina.text: [Apologetic] I volunteer before anyone asks, then later I am bitter that nobody sees how tired I am.
case-nina.suggestion: You offer before the request is even spoken, and later the tiredness has nowhere to be seen. I would like to stay with the cost that stayed invisible.

case-nina.text: [Torn] Next to other moms I shrink, like they all know a rule I missed.
case-nina.suggestion: Beside other mothers, you shrink around this sense that there is a rule you missed. Maybe we can stay with that outside feeling a little longer.

case-nina.text: [Tired] By bedtime I can't tell if I am sad, angry, or just completely used up.
case-nina.suggestion: By bedtime, sadness, anger, and exhaustion are tangled together. We can stay with the tangle before we try to name one strand.

case-nina.text: [Tearful, smiling] My colleague said I didn't have to earn the afternoon off. I laughed, but I wanted to cry. There was relief in hearing it.
case-nina.suggestion: You felt relief at not having to earn the rest. Could we slow down at that relief before the smile moves us past it?

case-nina.text: [Quietly] I was angry when they assumed I'd organise it again. Then I felt guilty. Even now, the guilt comes before I can finish saying I was angry.
case-nina.suggestion: The guilt arrives so quickly that the anger barely gets a sentence. We can pause and let you finish that sentence, without needing to act on it.

case-aisha.text: [Panicked] If a reply doesn't come, I tell myself it shouldn't matter, but then I can't focus on anything else.
case-aisha.suggestion: One part says it should not matter, and another part cannot let go of the missing reply. What do you notice in the part that cannot let go?

case-aisha.text: [Confused and embarrassed] I can ask someone not to leave and then want them away from me seconds later. I do not understand which part is actually me.
case-aisha.suggestion: Both movements are there: reaching and pushing away. What changes inside in the seconds between asking them to stay and wanting them gone?

case-aisha.text: [Desperate] When I scratch, part of me says it is not a big deal, and another part is scared you will judge me.
case-aisha.suggestion: One part makes the scratching small, and another part watches for my judgment. As you say that here, which part feels closer?

case-aisha.text: [Hurt and guarded] If you glance at the clock, I start wondering whether I should stop talking before you end it.
case-aisha.suggestion: The glance at the clock starts that pull to stop first, before I can end. What is the first feeling that comes up right then?

case-aisha.text: [Guarded] I ask people things I already half-know, just to see if they will give the answer in the right way.
case-aisha.suggestion: You are listening not only for the answer, but for whether it comes in the right way. What do you notice when it lands even slightly wrong?

case-aisha.text: [Desperate] When someone says goodbye, I know it is normal, but I get scared and angry at the same time.
case-aisha.suggestion: Goodbye brings fear and anger together, even while another part says it should be normal. At the word goodbye, which feeling arrives first?

case-aisha.text: [Panicked] Kindness makes me sob, and another part of me wants to bolt.
case-aisha.suggestion: Kindness brings sobbing and the urge to bolt at the same time. Where do you notice yourself first: in the sobbing, or in the pull to get away?

case-aisha.text: [Ashamed] When I remember what was done to me, I want to scrub my skin even though I know nothing is there.
case-aisha.suggestion: Remembering it brings a scrub-it-off feeling even when nothing is visible. What do you notice as that shame comes close here?

case-aisha.text: [Desperate] I keep checking the door, and I can't tell if I am angry you will leave or scared you might forget me.
case-aisha.suggestion: At the door there is anger and fear tangled together: leaving, being forgotten. As you look toward the door now, which side is closer?

case-aisha.text: [Hurt] If you cancel, a part of me says not to come back, even while another part wants to ask when you will be here again.
case-aisha.suggestion: Both parts appear around the cancellation: the part that wants to disappear and the part that needs to know there is still a place here. Where do you feel that split most strongly?

case-aisha.text: [Softer, watching the therapist] I was angry that you didn't agree with me. I'm still angry. But I'm also sad that I wanted your agreement so badly.
case-aisha.suggestion: The anger is still here, and sadness is appearing alongside it. We can take a little time with that sadness without asking the anger to disappear.

case-aisha.text: [Quiet, uneasy] I felt relieved when she said she'd call tomorrow. Then I couldn't let myself enjoy it. The relief is still there a little, though.
case-aisha.suggestion: A little relief is still available, even with the uneasiness. Could we notice just that small amount, without deciding what tomorrow will bring?

case-david.text: [Controlled] When she says I am cold, part of me wants to prove her wrong and another part wants to disappear.
case-david.suggestion: One part moves toward proving, another toward disappearing. What do you notice in the moment before either side takes over?

case-david.text: [Controlled] You seem calm when I talk about failure, and I cannot tell if I respect that or resent it.
case-david.suggestion: The calm you see lands in two ways at once: something respects it, and something resents it. Which side is louder as you talk about my calm?

case-david.text: [Defensive] When I feel judged, I smooth my shirt and start listing achievements.
case-david.suggestion: When judgment appears, the achievements come in quickly. What is the first signal that you are being judged, before the list starts?

case-david.text: [Controlled] Praise works for maybe ten seconds; then I start looking for the part they missed.
case-david.suggestion: The praise reaches you briefly, and then the search for what was missed takes over. Where does it stop landing?

case-david.text: [Dismissive] In hard talks, I check my phone the moment I feel cornered.
case-david.suggestion: When you feel cornered, the phone gives you a little distance. What is the cornered feeling like just before the phone comes out?

case-david.text: [Irritated] When my kids cry, I get impatient before I even know why.
case-david.suggestion: Your kids' tears bring impatience before you even know why. Where do you first notice that impatient surge?

case-david.text: [Wounded but sharp] Admitting I am wrong makes my face burn like everyone can see the failure.
case-david.suggestion: Admitting you are wrong brings heat to your face, like the failure is suddenly visible. What does that heat say in the moment before you cover it?

case-david.text: [Distant] Since the affair, I do not know whether I want forgiveness or to be left alone.
case-david.suggestion: There is a pull toward forgiveness and another toward being left alone. Which wish feels safer to let me see?

case-david.text: [Wounded but sharp] I want credit without having to ask, because asking makes me feel pathetic.
case-david.suggestion: You want the credit, and asking for it immediately brings that pathetic feeling close. Where does wanting recognition turn into shame?

case-david.text: [Controlled] When someone calls my work fine, I hear ordinary, and I cannot let it go.
case-david.suggestion: 'Fine' lands as ordinary, and ordinary becomes hard to tolerate. What do you notice in the instant before you need to prove more?

case-david.text: [Controlled, voice lowering] I was pleased they asked me to stay after the meeting. Not for advice. Just to have a drink with them. I don't usually say that matters.
case-david.suggestion: Being wanted for your company mattered. We can linger there for a moment, before you have to explain or minimise it.

case-david.text: [Quiet, guarded] My daughter says she misses me even when I'm home. I felt sad hearing that. Then I started explaining how much pressure I'm under.
case-david.suggestion: You noticed sadness before moving into the explanation. Could we return to just that moment of hearing she misses you?

case-marcus.text: [Slow and flat] Most days I'm numb, and then something hits me and I don't know what it is.
case-marcus.suggestion: The numbness holds, then something breaks through without a name. What do you notice at the first sign that something is coming?

case-marcus.text: [Hypervigilant] After nightmares, I know I should talk about them, but the details feel far away and I don't know where to start.
case-marcus.suggestion: The details stay far away, and the starting point keeps slipping. What do you notice as you try to begin?

case-marcus.text: [Quiet and guarded] Crowds make my shoulders rise, and I stay near the wall without deciding to.
case-marcus.suggestion: The wall seems to matter before you decide anything. What does being near it give you in that first second?

case-marcus.text: [Low voice] After dark I start wondering whether being alone is safer or just making me worse.
case-marcus.suggestion: Aloneness feels like protection and maybe harm at the same time. Which side of that question feels closer after dark?

case-marcus.text: [Low voice] After work I sit in the car because the apartment feels too quiet to enter.
case-marcus.suggestion: The car gives you a pause before the silent apartment. What does the quiet ask of you before you open the door?

case-marcus.text: [Quiet and guarded] I let calls go to voicemail because answering means I might have to explain why I am not okay.
case-marcus.suggestion: The ringing phone brings the possibility of having to explain. What feels too much in that first moment?

case-marcus.text: [Flat] Good moments happen, but I don't trust them enough to let them count.
case-marcus.suggestion: The good moment arrives, and mistrust interrupts before it can count. What happens right where it almost starts to matter?

case-marcus.text: [Low voice] A sudden sound cuts through me, and before I think, I am scanning the room.
case-marcus.suggestion: The sound cuts through, and the scanning starts before thought catches up. In the first second after the sound, where does your attention go?

case-marcus.text: [Quiet and guarded] I do not pick up when family calls because I do not want to find out what I feel.
case-marcus.suggestion: Letting the call go unanswered keeps the feeling away for a while. What starts to come close when you imagine answering?

case-marcus.text: [Flat] When people tell me I should not be alone so much, I say it is better this way, but I keep thinking about it after.
case-marcus.suggestion: Saying it is better this way protects you from something, and the thought still follows you. What do you notice after you say it?

case-marcus.text: [Low voice] I heard his favourite song. Usually I turn it off. This time I listened a bit. Felt sad. Not all at once.
case-marcus.suggestion: A little sadness came while you listened. We can stay with that little bit; we don't need the whole story.

case-marcus.text: [Guarded, pausing] When you didn't push for more, I was relieved. Still am. Hard to say that to someone.
case-marcus.suggestion: There's relief that I left you room. We can give that feeling a moment without asking you to say more than you want.
